correctness.rationale: For real 0<p<1 and p-metrics rho=d^p, the Cúth–Raunig finite spanning-tree norm formula reduces a signed three-terminal zero-mass vector to a weighted one-hub star; pruning zero-flow and suppressing degree-two nonterminal vertices preserves or decreases tree cost, and the finite-subset infimum covers arbitrary infinite superspaces. Thus ||mu||^p=inf_z∑|m_i|^p rho(t_i,z) and the intrinsic 3-point norm minimizes over terminal hubs. For arbitrary z, triangle inequalities yield norm_N^p≤S+min_i(A−2a_i)r_i≤(1+F^{-1})S, F=∑a_i/(A−2a_i)>0. For masses (−1,u,1−u), F≥t+1/(t−1)≥v+1/(v−1), where t=u^p+(1−u)^p≤v=2^(1−p)<2. The resulting factor 4/(4−2^(p+1)+2^(2p)) bounds every inverse norm. The explicit four-terminal star has rho arm lengths q^-1,q^-1,(2−q)^-1, masses (−2,1,1), realizes exact equality. Singleton molecule/zero mass and p approaching endpoints are handled; bounded symbolic and deterministic p tests corroborated exact ratio but are not the infinite-space proof.

value.rationale: Determines the exact worst-case inverse norm of the smallest genuinely nontrivial canonical Lipschitz-free p inclusion, settling an explicit 2023 lower-bound witness as sharp uniformly in p and unrestricted ambient cardinality. This gives a sharp benchmark for nonlocal convex embedding constants, motivated by the existing aa_p(2) extremal question rather than a contrived star instance.

limitations: Only real coefficients, 0<p<1, 3-point N, p-metric ambient spaces; no q>p or larger terminal classification.
